dedupe_keys.name: canadian cycling network database and canadian pedestrian network database statistics canada

description: The Canadian Cycling Network Database and the Canadian Pedestrian Network Database are national compilations of active transportation infrastructure produced by the Urban Data Lab at Statistics Canada with support from Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada. The cycling database harmonises municipal open data for 75 municipalities into the Canadian Bikeway Comfort and Safety (Can-BICS) classification, after more than 170 municipal portals were assessed, with data collected between November 2023 and February 2024. The pedestrian database classifies pedestrian infrastructure into eight categories. Together with the Canadian Public Transit Network Database they build on the Open Database of Infrastructure. Coverage is national but limited to municipalities that publish open data. Both are free under the Open Government Licence - Canada and are available as feature layers on ArcGIS Online and to download through Statistics Canada's Linkable Open Data Environment. Caveats: the harmonised networks inherit gaps and inconsistencies from municipal sources and are snapshots of 2023 to 2024. They support accessibility, active mobility and network analyses of walking and cycling, including agent-based demand models. They complement OpenStreetMap-based Can-BICS layers and are related to the Statistics Canada Open Database of Buildings.
